steps.name: Wire existing beep to new-high-score event
steps.definition_of_done: The existing single-beep round-robin fires when a run beats the stored high score, without adding sound assets or changing the audio API.
steps.notes: This is the smallest honest use of the current one-asset audio system. Collision-edge and GAME_OVER events already trigger the current beep through playNext(); the high-score branch now uses that same mechanism at the real record-break moment.
steps.implementation: In src/main.cpp, the high-score branch calls audio.playNext() before updating the in-memory score and saving it. No new asset, no new audio API, no sound-type abstraction was introduced.
steps.verification: Verified by Cyril: build succeeded, a full run reached 53.5884s and beat the prior high score of 47.7s; the console printed NEW HIGH SCORE and the beep was audible at that moment, alongside the existing catch/GAME_OVER triggers.

kill_criteria: If any step's scope keeps expanding instead of shrinking, stop, cut scope, and re-record a smaller definition_of_done before continuing. Do not introduce an abstraction, manager, registry, or subsystem unless the current implementation demonstrates a concrete need for it.
